To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
c-Jun immunostainings are increased in the intermediate zone in the spinal cord and in the brainstem reticulare formation in SOD1 mice.

the number of c-Jun-immune neurons was decreased in the motoneuron pool of the spinal cord in SOD1 (G93A mice due to motoneuron loss, while the number of cJun-immune neurons in the brainstem reticulare formation and in the intermediate zone in the spinal cord were increased in SOD1 mice due to cJun induction.

In a transgenic mouse line carrying a superoxide dismutas 1 (Sod1) gene with a glycine-93 to alanine mutation (G93A), the expression of c-Jun, a transcription factor frequently upregulated in injured neurons, was increased in neurons in the spinal cord and in the brainstem of the mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms involved in motoneuron death.
the induction of c-jun immunoreactivity in motoneurons and other neurons in the spinal cord and brain stem in transgenic SOD(G93A) mouse model for motoneuron disease.
the development of novel therapies for the treatment of ALS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the c-Jun induction in the intermediate zone and reticular formation of the spinal cord in SOD1 (G93A)-transgenic mice, as well as the increased levels of c-Jun found in ALS-patients, is a consequence of the degeneration of the motor neurons.
c-Jun is induced in neurons throughout the CNS of SOD1(G933A) mice and this induction is most pronounced in neurons in the brainstem reticulospinal tract and in motoneurons of the ventral horn.
the induction of c-Jun immunostainings in SOD1 mice is not specific for ALS but rather is a general response of motoneurons to degeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
c-Jun immunoreactivitiy is induced in the spinal cord and brain of transgenic mice with ALS-linked SOD1 mutations.
c-Jun immunoreactivities are strongly induced in neurons of the intermediate zone and the brainstem reticulofugal system of the SOD1(G9A3) mice.
the c-Jun expression in the intermediate zone may be an early marker for ALS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the induction of c-Jun in SOD1 mutant mice may be an early marker of neurodegeneration.
c-Jun is induced in motoneurons and in neurons of the spinal cord (intermediate zone) and brainstem reticular neurons in a transgenetic model for ALS.
the c-Jun immunoreaction is induced in the intermediate zone in SOD1 mice, which could be a marker of neurodegeneration.
